requirements.text: The block works for every `W` from 4 to 32, and bits `W` and up of the `LOAD` and `COUNT` registers read as zero; a write to `LOAD` ignores them.
While `rst_n` is low at a rising edge of `clk`, `CTRL`, `LOAD`, `COUNT` and `STATUS` clear to zero.
A write to `CTRL` stores `wdata` bits 2 to 0 in it, and a write to `LOAD` stores `wdata` bits `W-1` to 0 in it.
A read never changes any register; `rdata` follows `addr` with no clock edge.
At a rising edge where a write to `CTRL` sets `EN` and `EN` was 0, the count loads the `LOAD` value.
At a rising edge where `EN` is 1 and the count is not zero, and no write to `CTRL` takes place, the count falls by one.
A write to `CTRL` takes the place of that edge's count step: at that edge the count does not fall and the timer does not expire, whatever the count was.
A write to `CTRL` that clears `EN` stops the timer and the count keeps its value.
A write to `LOAD` does not change the count: the new value is used at the next start or periodic reload.
At a rising edge where `EN` is 1 and the count is zero, and no write to `CTRL` takes place, the timer expires: `EXPIRED` is set.
In periodic mode an expiry also loads the count with the `LOAD` value, and `EN` stays 1.
In one-shot mode an expiry also clears `EN`, and the count stays zero until the next start.
A write to `STATUS` with bit 0 set clears `EXPIRED`, and with bit 0 clear changes nothing; it never sets the flag.
A timer that expires at the same rising edge as a write that clears `EXPIRED` keeps `EXPIRED` set.
`irq` is high exactly when `EXPIRED` and `IE` are both 1, in one-shot and periodic mode alike; it follows the registers with no clock edge.

items.name: Reset values and reset from a busy state
items.rationale: Both lanes read every register after the first reset and again after a reset with the timer running, expired and its interrupt up.

items.name: CTRL and LOAD write and read back
items.rationale: Patterns and all ones are written and read back at W 16 and W 5; bits a register does not store, and bits W and up of LOAD and COUNT, must read zero.

items.name: Reads change nothing
items.rationale: Registers are read twice between edges and must not move; every read is sampled with no clock edge, and a COUNT write changes nothing.

items.name: Start loads the count
items.rationale: A start loads the stored LOAD value; a stop holds the count over several edges, and a second start loads LOAD again.

items.name: The count falls one per edge
items.rationale: The count is read after each edge down to zero; a LOAD write while the timer runs must leave the count falling by one.

items.name: A CTRL write takes an edge's place
items.rationale: With the count at zero and the timer running, a CTRL write must set no flag at its edge; the expiry comes at the next one.

items.name: Expiry sets the flag
items.rationale: The flag stays clear while the count runs and is set at the edge after the count reaches zero, in both modes.

items.name: Periodic expiry reloads
items.rationale: After an expiry in periodic mode EN still reads 1 and the count holds the LOAD value, including a LOAD written after the start.

items.name: One-shot expiry stops
items.rationale: After an expiry in one-shot mode EN reads 0 and the count stays zero over several edges, and no second expiry follows a clear.

items.name: Write-1-to-clear
items.rationale: A STATUS write of bit 0 clears the flag; a write with bit 0 clear, or of all ones to a clear flag, never sets or clears it.

items.name: Expiry at the edge of a clear
items.rationale: A periodic timer with a zero reload expires at every edge; a STATUS clear at one of them must leave the flag set.

items.name: Interrupt masked by IE in each mode
items.rationale: irq is checked with IE clear and set, in one-shot and in periodic mode separately, each 1 ns after the edge that expires or clears, with no extra edge.
